articles.title: 3 members of family from PH fatally stabbed in California | ABS-CBN News
articles.text: A tragic incident involving a family from the Philippines in Baldwin Park, California, has left three family members dead, including two children, in what police describe as a brutal stabbing attack. Authorities have arrested a 23-year-old male suspect, who is believed to be related to the victims. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner identified the victims as 8-year-old Mia Chantelle Narvaez, 16-year-old Paul Sebastian Manangan, and 44-year-old Rona Nate. All three victims sustained fatal stab wounds to the upper body. Filipino siblings, 2 others shot dead in Southern California home According to a press release by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Baldwin Park police responded to a disturbance call on the 4700 block of Bogart Avenue on the evening of December 26. The suspect attempted to flee in a vehicle but crashed into a cul-de-sac before being detained. He was later booked for murder. Out of respect for the victims’ families, authorities have not disclosed the exact nature of the relationship between the suspect and the victims. However, investigators confirmed that the suspect lived at the residence. POLICE SEEK MORE INFORMATION ON INCIDENT According to local news reports , neighbors recounted chilling details of the incident, including the screams of a young girl running for help. “You heard the little girl screaming, coming out and crying for help, saying, ‘Someone call 911. My brother stabbed my mom in the back, I saw blood,’” shared Nathan Garcia to ABC7 news. Another neighbor, Edna Figueroa, expressed shock and fear over the incident, describing it as “a very scary feeling… to find out that this is happening in our neighborhood.” The family is believed to have Filipino roots, with neighbors confirming their shared heritage. The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Homicide Bureau is assisting Baldwin Park police with the ongoing investigation. The case will be presented to the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office for review and potential filing of charges. Authorities urge anyone with information about the incident to contact the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Homicide Bureau at (323) 890-5500. Anonymous tips can also be submitted through “Crime Stoppers” at (800) 222-TIPS (8477) or via the P3 Tips mobile app. Meanwhile, a GoFundMe page has been created to "help the family grieve properly and say their goodbyes to their loved ones." articles.title: 29-year-old patient dies after three procedures at cosmetic clinic
articles.text:
A 29-year-old patient died after undergoing three aesthetic procedures at a clinic on Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong City, Cedric Castillo reported on 24 Oras.

Shiryl Saturnino was reported on Tuesday to have died at The Icon Clinic hours after she entered its operating room at 5 p.m. on Saturday for a liposuction, butt, and breast augmentation.

The Icon Clinic's staff noticed that Saturnino no longer had a pulse at 3 a.m. on Sunday after all her procedures have been completed.

Mandaluyong City Police Chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said the doctor who performed Saturnino's operation called for an ambulance from the Makati Medical Center and tried to revive her but failed.

"Triny nilang ma-revive 'to around 2:40 pero nag-expire siya mga 3:21," Alva said.

Operating doctors Dr. Jose Jovito Mendiola and Dr. Samuel Yapjuangco, circulating nurse Virgil Alec Ongleo, nurse assistant Alvin Carl Genove, and staff nurse Audrey Michelle have submitted their licenses and documents to the police.

Alva clarified that they have yet to identify a suspect behind Saturnino's death.

"Kinausap ng mga investigator ko yung mga doctor. Kaya lang nagpeprepare pa sila ng statement, nagpapa-assist sila sa lawyer nila," he explained. "Ang pinaka magiging matibay na batayan natin ay yung resulta ng autopsy."

Saturnino's parents had no idea that her emergency was connected to aesthetic procedures until they found her dead.

"(Nadatnan namin) sa operating room. Pagdating namin ayun, nakatakip na siya ng ano, kumot. Actually, hindi ko alam na ganun yung daratnan ko, akala ko buhay pa siya," Sherly, Saturnino's mother, said.

"Wala po kaming alam. Lahat po nun, ng procedure po niya, wala po kaming alam," she continued.

Dante Anabe, Saturnino's uncle, said the family came to the clinic on Tuesday afternoon to ask for a refund for her niece's procedures.

"Inalam namin kung how much did she pay, so nalaman namin kung magkano then we requested for a refund. And then granted naman yung refund," Anabe said.

Saturnino's family may press charges against The Icon Clinic.

"We're contemplating on that, we're just waiting for the result of the histopathology exam," Anabe said.

The Icon Clinic's legal counsel, Atty. Estelita D. Cordero, stressed that it was working with the police and Saturnino's family in addition to requesting five working days to submit affidavits pertinent to the case.

She added that Saturnino had been a regular patient for years and was cherished by the clinic.

"Ginagawa po namin ang lahat at kasalukuyan po kaming nakikipagtulungan sa abot ng aming makakaya upang malaman kung ano ang totoong nangyayari sa 'di inaasahang pagpanaw ni Bb. Saturnino," Cordero wrote.

She added, "Si Bb. Saturnino ay ilang taong nang regular pasyente ng The Icon Clinic at labis naming ikinalulungkot ang kanyang sinapit." —Rie Takumi/NB, GMA News

articles.title: Shiryl Saturnino died of multiple organ failure after 3 cosmetic procedures —autopsy report
articles.text:
Multiple organ failure secondary to complications of cosmetic surgery was the cause of death stated on the autopsy report of businesswoman Shiryl Anabe Saturnino, who died at The Icon Clinic in Mandaluyong City on Sunday.

Emil Sumangil reported on 24 Oras that these findings were presented during the case conference of Special Investigation Task Group Shiryl on Thursday.

If Saturnino's death is proven to be the result of their neglect, Dr. Samuel Eric Calderon Yapjuangco, anesthesiologist Dr. Jose Jovito Cordero Mendiola and nurses Virgil Alec Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove, and Audrey Michelle Santos will face criminal and administrative cases.

"Nakikita kong may negligence on part of The Icon Clinic, considering na yung initial requirements para mag-exist ang isang medical clinic ay hindi nila nasunod," SITG Shiryl Commander P/Sr. Supt. Marcelino Pedrozo said.

"We are contemplating to file reckless imprudence resulting to homicide," Pedrozo added. "That will lead to the reprimand, suspension, and revocation of the license of the doctors or the nurses involved."

The task force ruled to have Saturnino's histopathology examination prioritized at the PNP crime lab to allow them to charge medical personnel involved in her fatal surgery.

"At least nakausap na natin yung mga medical doctors natin. Although may resulta na sa autopsy ang recommendation nila, hintayin pa talaga yung hispathological examination dahil mas detalyado yun," Mandaluyong Police chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said.

Among other pieces of evidence police are considering in the case are the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) IDs presented by doctors and nurses.

Saturnino's medical records since her first medical procedure at The Icon Clinic in 2013 and a letter of consent signed by the victim were also presented during the case conference.

Dr. Briccio G. Alcantara, Philippine Association of Plastic Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons Vice-President for Internal Affairs, said their group will also investigate Saturnino's death.

"Even a minor surgery under local, even in a medium surgery, there will always be a complication. And that complication is usually minimized by having exams na fit ang patient. Miniminimize but it may still happen," Alcantara said.

Neither Japjuangco nor Cordero have given a statement on the police's latest findings. —Rie Takumi/JST, GMA News

articles.title: Beauty clinic charged for woman’s death
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines - Two doctors and three nurses of a beauty clinic were charged with reckless imprudence resulting in homicide before the Mandaluyong City prosecutor’s office yesterday in connection with a businesswoman’s death while undergoing cosmetic surgery. Police said Samuel Eric Yapjuangco was the anesthesiologist while Jose Jovito Mendiola performed breast augmentation, liposuction and Brazilian buttock lift on Sheryl Saturnino, 29, on March 26. Nurses Virgil Alex Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove and Audrey Michelle Santos assisted during the operation. Chief Superintendent Romulo Sapitula, Eastern Police District director, said the EPD submitted as evidence Saturnino’s death certificate, pathology results and testimonies of several witnesses. In filing the case yesterday, investigators were accompanied by Saturnino’s mother and family lawyer Ruel Asubar. articles.title: Ginang nasawi matapos ang 4 na cosmetic surgery
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — Iniimbestigahan ng National Bureau of Investigation-Homicide Division ang pagkamatay ng isang ginang na sumailalim sa liposuction, tummy tuck, Brazilian butt lift, at bodytite for arms ng isang celebrity plastic surgeon, sa San Juan City noong Marso, 2, 2026. Ang American-based Filipino-American reality television na si Ronn Tristan Perez, anak ng nasawi, ang personal na nagtungo sa NBI noong Huwebes. Batay sa mga ulat, ang biktimang si Gng. Casteel ay nagbayad ng P570,000 para sa nasabing procedures na umabot ng pitong oras, na-discharge matapos ang 3 araw na recovery period. Subalit pagkalipas ng apat na araw ay isinugod siya sa ospital at na-diagnosed ng “high-risk pulmonary embolisim” o isang medical emergency dahil sa blood clot na humarang sa daloy ng dugo sa baga at mapanganib na hindi normal na presyon ng dugo. Nag-aalala aniya, siya sa nakitang hitsura ng ina nang makausap sa Face Time habang nasa klinika. “I FaceTime her, and she’s pale, she’s missing a tooth. I said, ‘What’s happening, Mom?’ Me and my brother were both worried,” ani Perez. Ilang araw ang lumipas nang makatanggap siya ng tawag mula sa tiyo at ama na binawian ng buhay ang ina. Hindi aniya, niya nakuha ang gusto niyang makita nang ibigay ang medical records ng ina. “I’m not accusing anyone of anything. I need more than that. I need documents, papers, expertise that what was done here is everything that was supposed to be done. No stones left unturned,” aniya sa isang interview. Payo niya sa sinumang nais magpa-enhance o magpaganda na kahit mabilis na pag-Google lang ay dapat munang alamin ang mga delikadong bagay at magdoble ingat habang ginagawa at pagkatapos ng procedures. articles.title: Mourning the lack of collective outrage
articles.text: EVERY Undas or All Souls Day (Nov. 2) when Filipinos troop to cemeteries to remember departed loved ones, I always think of the families of desaparecidos. Where do they go to offer flowers and light the candles for their dead whom they didn’t bury? I think of Edith Burgos, whose son Jonas was last seen on April 28, 2007 at the Ever Gotesco Mall. I think of University of the Philippines students Sherlyn Cadapan and Karen Empeno who were last seen on June 26, 2006 in Hagonoy, Bulacan. There are many more: Father Rudy Romano, a Redemptorist priest who served landless peasants and displaced settlers and the six workers of Paper Industries Corporation of the Philippines namely Joseph Belar, Jovencio Lagare, Romualdo Orcullo, Diosdado Oliver, Artemio Ayala Jr. and Arnold Dangkiasan. The list is long according to Asian Federation against Involuntary Disappearances (AFAD) and Families of Victims of Involuntary Disappearance (FIND) “For the families whose loved ones were made to disappear by their own governments, remembering the disappeared is a painful and torturous ordeal. They have no graves to visit, no tombs to light candles and no place to offer flowers. Even silence is an elusive desire to pray as the cry of their disappeared loved ones for truth and justice occupies their memories,” said Darwin Mendiola, AFAD project coordinator. This All Souls Day, I think of the 3,000 or more who were recently killed in President Duterte’s war against drugs. Last Saturday, the family of 34-year old Florjohn Cruz laid him to rest 10 days after he was killed in a round-up of suspected “pushers” in Caloocan City last Oct. 19. A cardboard with words, “Pusher at Adik, Huwag Tularan” was found near his dead body. Like many others who were killed the last three months since Duterte took power, the family said Cruz, a singer-musician, a hockey player and a dean’s lister in a computer school, had been hooked in drugs but he never engaged in drug pushing, He didn’t have a gun which belied police allegation that he was killed because he shot the arresting policemen. It’s double tragedy for the Rosales family who are still mourning the killing of their son Petronio Rosales Jr last October 26 while waiting for a ride in front of a restaurant along Yakal Street in Barangay San Antonio, Makati. Jhay-R, as Petronio is known to relatives and friends, has been living in the United Kingdom and came home when his sister Lauren was killed while riding in a jeepney last July. The killing was reported as related to the government’s campaign against illegal drugs. The family vehemently protests saying Lauren, an executive assistant in a food company, was never into illegal drugs. The culprits were never known nor arrested. Jhay-R, an IT expert, was reportedly following up Lauren’s Social Security Service benefits before he goes back to UK when he was killed last week. A retired policeman, Alfredo Jebulan, is very angry. His son, Yani, a student at Our Lady of Fatima University in Caloocan was shot to death by riding- in- tandem men wearing bonnets at around 12 midnight Oct. 29 2016. He said his son was not into drugs. He wrote a letter to President Duterte raging: “My point is, if I will know that one of your policemen has the hand for the cause of the death of my son, God forbids, I will let heaven and earth befall upon him. I know you don’t tolerate this but let me be very very frank, if they know how to kill people, so am I. This goes to you too Gen. Dela Rosa Sir. I’m begging you Help me solve the unnecessary death of my son PLEASE or I will be the one to do it without your help.” Jebulan’s letter is being shared in social media. But that is all. The killings continue. Enjoying “very good” satisfaction rating for his first 100 days performance dominated by killings unprecedented in the country’s history, Duterte vowed to kill more. “I tell you, I will triple it. ‘Pag hindi nasunod ang gusto ko, to get rid of my country (of the drug problem), you can expect 20,000 or 30,000 more (deaths),” Duterte said last week. News reports of killings, either by police officers or by vigilantes, have become a daily norm. People are no longer shocked. Poet Marne Kilates wrote in Facebook : “SAD. REALLY sad to see friends and acquaintances of apparently considerable intellectual capacity slip into the Pied Piper’s parade of lightweight flute music, or more frighteningly, into the discombobulated rationalizations for what really is the rantings of a deranged leader canonized by electoral process and the subsequent adulation and fawning of mass insanity.” “They forget, “ Marne rued, “in the process, the most basic features of a civilized community and a working democracy: the Rule of Law, Due Process, and Human Rights, Human Rights, Human Rights. They bristle and scamper away at the mere mention of these civilized concepts, like the aswangs of folklore when shown a crucifix. They are afraid of these concepts because they don’t know how to deal with them. Or these remind them that they are in fact in the wrong and would not admit it. They have regressed into the state of the not-so-noble savage pre-Enlightenment and pre-Renaissance, rushed across time and plunged into the all-gaming, all-dominating, and all-deceiving neo-fascist Gehenna of the Dark Internet.” We have lost our sense of outrage. We should be in a state of mourning. Receive fresh perspectives and explainers in your inbox every Tuesday and Friday. articles.title: Enough of 'Alice Guos'!
articles.text: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. The numbers are appalling! Two hundred Chinese nationals with fake birth certificates and 3.7 million Filipinos without birth certificates, of whom 1.4 million are ages 14 and younger. It’s about time Congress acted swiftly on a pending bill that will ease the registration of births, marriages and deaths of Filipinos and penalize those who take advantage of the system’s weaknesses. The last comprehensive national law on civil registration, Republic Act 3753, or the Civil Registration Law, was enacted more than 90 years ago, in November 1930. The Philippine Legislators’ Committee on Population and Development Foundation (PLCPD) presented to the media last July 12 the salient features of the pending legislation, which has become relevant in view of the revelations in the Senate probe on the alleged involvement of suspended Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Leal Guo in unlawful activities connected with the operations of the Philippine offshore gaming operation (POGO) hub in her town. From the Senate probe, it appears that Guo had a late registration of birth in November 2005, when she was 19 years old. As a consequence, the senators discovered several other irregularities in the process that made it apparently easy for the Bamban mayor to obtain Filipino citizenship. Sen. Sherwin Gatchalian said on Friday that foreigners managed to acquire Filipino citizenship practically overnight simply by paying P300,000 in exchange for a fraudulent birth certificate and driving license. He said this was the modus operandi uncovered by the National Bureau of Investigation involving 200 Chinese nationals who were able to secure certificates of live birth in 2018 and 2019 alone from the civil registry of Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur province. Because of this, Gatchalian is seeking a suspension of the policy that allows late registration of birth. But the PLCPD, a group of forward-looking lawmakers and advocates working on policies related to population and human development, noted that late registration is mostly in remote and disadvantaged areas where the process of acquiring a birth certificate is hindered by distance, low literacy or financial constraints. “Without a birth certificate, a child or an individual faces the risk of being denied [the] rights to identity, education, health services, inheritance, employment, and even legal justice in cases where determining the age is crucial,” Romeo Dongeto, executive director of PLCPD, explained. A birth certificate is usually required for school enrolment or when applying for a job, licenses, passport and other identification documents. “A birth certificate is every Filipino child’s passport to their hopes and dreams. We need to pass the Civil Registration bill to make birth registration free and accessible, especially for the most vulnerable Filipinos,” Dongeto said. The measure also involves modernizing and digitizing the civil registration system, as well as establishing barangay-level registration to reach more marginalized sectors. Registration of marriages and deaths is as important as legal documentation of births. Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) show that many deaths go unreported due to logistical hurdles and cultural practices, particularly in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), where only 42% of deaths were registered in 2021. Dennis Mapa, national statistician and civil registrar general, said an omnibus bill on civil registration and vital statistics is “long overdue and should be a legislative priority” to improve further the efficiency of the delivery of civil registration services as well as ensure the integrity of civil registry documents in the civil registry offices. “A death certificate is needed for surviving family members to access inheritance, social pensions, insurance and burial assistance. With an improved and accessible civil registration system, the government can properly assist these individuals and ensure that their rights are being upheld,” said lawyer Sophia Monica San Luis, a civil registry global expert. Sen. Risa Hontiveros, principal author of the Civil Registration bill in the Senate, said the falsification of civil registry documents, which is what the Guo family apparently did, must be stopped. “Our current investigation has revealed deep cracks in our systems that need correcting. It also exposed the ways our institutions have been corrupted by unscrupulous individuals who want to exploit the weaknesses of our people. The most vulnerable in society are affected by the lack of an efficient and honest civil registration and vital statistics system,” said Hontiveros, who is leading the probe into Guo’s alleged involvement in the POGOs’ illegal operations. “Delayed registration of birth happens,” she acknowledged, noting that this is a significant concern, especially among Filipinos who lack the financial means to obtain a birth certificate. However, she said: “It’s a different story if the weaknesses of our system are being abused, like in the case of the Guo family. A streamlined and strengthened civil registration and vital statistics system is needed to safeguard the safety, nationality and citizenship of the most vulnerable Filipinos.” To Tingog party-list Rep. Jude Acidre, a deputy majority leader at the House and one of the bill’s authors, emphasized that the benefits of an improved civil registration system do not end with the individual’s ability to access their rights; they also translate into foundational data that supports national progress. “If every birth or vital event of a Filipino is registered, we can generate accurate data. With accurate data, we can make evidence-based policies and decisions to ensure that no one is being left behind,” he pointed out. Health Department Undersecretary Emmie Liza Perez-Chiong, for her part, said reforming the civil registration system will address the huge gaps in the availability and quality of critical data on vital events of a person, including birth, marriage and death. Having accurate data is crucial in national health policy and planning and coordinating services for the Filipino population at all levels of the country’s health care system. Risa Hontiveros, principal author of the Civil Registration bill in the Senate, said the falsification of civil registry documents, which is what the Guo family apparently did, must be stopped. “Our current investigation has revealed deep cracks in our systems that need correcting. It also exposed the ways our institutions have been corrupted by unscrupulous individuals who want to exploit the weaknesses of our people. The most vulnerable in society are affected by the lack of an efficient and honest civil registration and vital statistics system,” said Hontiveros, who is leading the probe into Guo’s alleged involvement in the POGOs’ illegal operations. “Delayed registration of birth happens,” she acknowledged, noting that this is a significant concern, especially among Filipinos who lack the financial means to obtain a birth certificate. However, she said: “It’s a different story if the weaknesses of our system are being abused, like in the case of the Guo family. A streamlined and strengthened civil registration and vital statistics system is needed to safeguard the safety, nationality and citizenship of the most vulnerable Filipinos.” To Tingog party-list Rep. Jude Acidre, a deputy majority leader at the House and one of the bill’s authors, emphasized that the benefits of an improved civil registration system do not end with the individual’s ability to access their rights; they also translate into foundational data that supports national progress. “If every birth or vital event of a Filipino is registered, we can generate accurate data. With accurate data, we can make evidence-based policies and decisions to ensure that no one is being left behind,” he pointed out. Health Department Undersecretary Emmie Liza Perez-Chiong, for her part, said reforming the civil registration system will address the huge gaps in the availability and quality of critical data on vital events of a person, including birth, marriage and death. Having accurate data is crucial in national health policy and planning and coordinating services for the Filipino population at all levels of the country’s health care system. articles.title: PROFILE: Who is Melvin Matibag, the prosecution’s final witness on alleged threats? | ABS-CBN News
articles.text: NBI Director Melvin Matibag takes the witness stand on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment trial and continues on Wednesday. Matibag is the prosecution’s final witness for the fourth article, which accuses Duterte of committing grave threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and his relatives and inciting to sedition through said alleged threats. Impeachment Trial of Sara Duterte His appearance came months after he was appointed as NBI chief. Before joining the Marcos administration, however, Matibag was considered an ally of the vice president’s father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, having held several key posts during the previous administration. A TEACHERS’ SON Matibag’s parents began their careers as teachers before later joining government service. His father taught at Claro M. Recto High School, while his mother served as a teacher at Pedro Pelaez Elementary School. He is married to Laguna First District Rep. Ma. Rene Ann Matibag. A lawyer by profession, Matibag earned his undergraduate degree in Philosophy from the University of Santo Tomas before obtaining his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University in 1996. He was admitted to the Philippine bar the following year and later completed a master’s degree in corporate and finance law at Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan. TIES TO THE DUTERTES Former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo appointed Matibag as general manager of the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) in 2010. In 2014, he served as convenor of Movement for Reform, Continuity and Momentum (More2Come), a group that advocated to amend the 1987 Constitution to allow then-President Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III to seek another term. In 2017, the older Duterte appointed Matibag as president of the National Transmission Corporation (TransCo). Matibag later became acting secretary-general of Duterte’s political party, Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban), during a leadership dispute that split the party into two. In 2022, Duterte appointed him as acting cabinet secretary, a position that was later abolished by the Marcos administration. Matibag resigned as PDP-Laban acting secretary-general in 2023, saying his personal principles were no longer aligned with the party's direction. He also said he wanted to avoid any appearance of a conflict of interest because his wife belonged to a different political party. TIMELINE: The cracks in ruling party PDP-Laban before BBM endorsement OPINION PIECES AGAINST DUTERTE After leaving PDP-Laban, Matibag returned to private law practice and entered the academe, becoming the first dean of the Lyceum of Alabang College of Law. He also became a columnist for the Daily Tribune, where he wrote about the vice president. In October 2023, Matibag wrote in his column that he opposed the allocation of confidential and intelligence funds to the Office of the Vice President. He argued that the Constitution does not assign the vice president functions that would require such funds. At the time, he emphasized that his position was directed at the policy rather than Vice President Duterte personally. But nearly a year later, Matibag criticized Duterte in a September 2024 column and described her as a “bratinella” or a spoiled brat. In November of the same year, following Duterte’s controversial livestream that formed part of the impeachment case against her, Matibag published another opinion column. Matibag criticized Duterte’s remarks in the livestream and described her actions as “an ambitious power grab” that resulted in her “humiliating defeat.” He also again referred to her as a “bratinella.” At the impeachment trial, Matibag explained that it was the older Duterte who first used the moniker for her daughter, the vice president. SHIFT TO THE MARCOS ADMINISTRATION In September 2024, Matibag filed a disbarment complaint against former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque, a staunch ally of the Dutertes and his colleague during the Duterte administration. Matibag said the complaint included issues related to Roque's social media posts, including the so-called “polvoron” video involving Marcos. In August 2025, Matibag sought to return to government service by applying for the vacant position of Ombudsman but was not selected for the post. Instead, Marcos appointed him NBI director on February 19, 2026. This is also in the same period that a second round of impeachment complaints against Duterte were filed at the House of Representatives. Following his appointment, some questioned whether his selection was linked to his complaint against Roque. Matibag denied the allegation, saying his appointment was “not a reward.” Marcos to name ex-PDP exec Melvin Matibag as new NBI chief New NBI chief says appointment 'not a reward'

articles.title: Impeach trial Day 9: Matibag cross-examination to continue | ABS-CBN News
articles.text: Defense counsel Mark Vinluan cross-examines National Bureau of Investigation Melvin Matibag on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team on Wednesday will continue the cross-examination of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on the ninth day of her impeachment trial. Constitutional law expert Domingo Egon Cayosa cautioned the defense about how to cross-examine a “competent witness” like Matibag. “Binabalik niya yung tanong at dinadagdagan pa niya,” Cayosa reasoned. “Meron pa siyang counter-attack. Normally, a witness doesn’t do that. Sasagutin lang tanong mo. Siya, binabalik niya at dinadagdagan pa niya,” he told DZMM. On Tuesday, House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro quizzed Matibag on the NBI's investigation into the alleged threats that Duterte made against Marcos Jr. and his relatives, including the possibility that she already had an arrangement with someone to do so. Matibag, like previous witnesses from the NBI, said the bureau took Duterte's statements seriously because of the potential threat to national security. He added that the NBI already had persons of interest — people who may be involved in an investigation but who are not suspects — but said he could not disclose who they are. LASCAÑAS AFFIDAVIT The prosecution on Tuesday also showed a 2011 video of Duterte punching a court sheriff when she was still Davao City mayor and featured an excerpt of alleged Davao Death Squad hitman Arturo Lascañas' affidavit on drug-related killings to repeated objections from defense counsel Mark Vinluan. Defense counsel Mark Vinluan stressed his team's objection to the Lascañas affidavit, which was submitted to the International Criminal Court but that Matibag had no personal knowledge on. "We cannot allow this witness to build his testimony based on this document," Vinluan also said, pointing out the affidavit is unsigned and was not notarized. Luistro said the video and the affidavit were material since the NBI considered these in its investigation. Matibag also referred to the affidavit as "open source intelligence" that the NBI used for leads. Trial presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero allowed the presentation of the affidavit but reminded senators that its contents were not necessarily true and that the impeachment court was not saying that they were. MATIBAG WIFE During cross-examination, Vinluan raised that Matibag is married to Laguna First District Rep. Ann Matibag, one of the House members who supported Duterte's impeachment. The NBI director said his wife's job "is totally detached" from his official duties. House prosecution panel spokesman Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said Wednesday Rep. Matibag's work should not be used to cast doubt on the NBI investigation. “Obviously, the congresswoman has a different role from the work of the NBI chief,” Adiong told ANC's "Headstart". Adiong also defended Matibag’s writing of several anti-Duterte opinion columns prior to his stint as NBI chief, noting that the investigation was already ongoing before his appointment. Asked if the columns showed that Matibag had long been biased against Duterte, he said, “He shared his opinion but that did not negate the fact that the Vice President did utter those words…Whether or not Matibag has several leanings is not the subject matter of the investigation.” The NBI director is the last prosecution witness on Duterte's alleged threats. DEFENSE ‘HAPPY’ WITH INITIAL CROSS Meanwhile, Duterte’s defense team believes that “at least for this first half of the cross-examination, we were able to again meet our targets,” said panel spokesperson Atty. Michael Poa. “So, masaya naman kami sa nangyari. But definitely, hindi pa tayo tapos. So, itutuloy pa natin…and we'll see how things go,” Poa told reporters. Poa said they were testing the credibility of the NBI chief but added it was up to the impeachment court to say whether Matibag was a credible witness or not. “Well, that's really for the court to appreciate. Pero siyempre, ang point namin talaga is to test the credibility, Test kung may bias man o wala,” he said. TRUST RATING Poa also explained Vinluan’s line of questioning and the relevance of survey results showing the trust ratings of Duterte to the allegations of betrayal of public trust. “Pinakita lang naman natin na kung betrayal of public trust ang pinag-uusapan ng tao, yung tiwala ng tao sa ating Bise Presidente, pinakita lang natin at tinanong lang natin. Ang point lang naman nun is tinanong lang natin kung yung mga ganong bagay ay kino-consider din ng NBI sa kanilang investigation lalo na parating nababanggit yung katagang betrayal of public trust kanina,” Poa said. Poa added that the Lacañas documents were not an affidavit but a private document. “Kung it's a private document, then you have to prove that it was in fact duly executed or may due execution. Pag notaryado kasi, nagiging public document na siya. Whereas pag walang notaryo, private document lang siya. That's why sa amin, hindi namin siya tinatawag na affidavit kasi magiging affidavit lang naman ‘pag sumumpa ka sa katotohanan ng mga sinasabi mo, that goes for everyone. And dito sa instances na ito, hindi kasi nangyari yun,” he said. Poa also explained the team’s strategy to put an “x” mark on the documents presented during the trial and said this was not meant to mislead the public. “There was no intention to mislead the public. Ang point lang namin dun is gusto lang natin pakita through graphics kung ano yung may personal knowledge siya, ano yung wala. Para lang mas madaling ma-appreciate na itong dokumento na ito, wala kang personal knowledge. Itong pangalawang dokumento, wala rin siyang personal knowledge. It's really to show aling dokumento yung may personal knowledge sa wala,” he said. ‘HINDI NATIBAG’ Meanwhile, the House prosecution so far sees “no reason” to conduct a redirect examination on Matibag, according to one of its counsels, Atty. Benjamin Tolosa Jr. “So far, doon sa mga naging tanong kahapon, parang wala kaming nakikitang masyadong rason para kailangan pang mag-redirect, lalu na’t… hindi natibag ang naging statement ni NBI director kahapon,” Tolosa said. The prosecution also does not see a need to take back its previous manifestation to drop some witnesses for the impeachment article accusing Duterte of making grave threats. “When we said we can already waive the presentation of some of the witnesses... based ‘yan sa aming assessment na hindi na sila kailangan, dahil ‘yung kanilang intended testimony ay na-cover na ng mga naging testimonya ng aming mga naunang witnesses,” he said. — With a report from Jonathan De Santos, ABS-CBN News Defense counsel Mark Vinluan cross-examines National Bureau of Investigation Melvin Matibag on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag gave his testimony on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. Batangas 2nd District Rep. Gerville Luistro, lead House prosecutor, quizzed Matibag on the NBI's investigation into the alleged threats that Duterte made against Marcos Jr. and his relatives, including the possibility that she already had an arrangement with someone to do so. During her examination of Matibag, Luistro had a video of Duterte's brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte speaking at a political rally in April where he seemed to call for Marcos Jr.'s head. Matibag said the video was relevant to the probe because it showed the vice president's 2024 statements were "a kinetic force" and that some who heard the alleged threats took her cue and made their own threats. Matibag told: ‘Avoid statements pertaining to members of impeachment court’ The NBI director said more than 600,000 people viewed the video of Mayor Duterte's statements, which he said shows the reach of the alleged threat. Matibag, like previous witnesses from the NBI, said the bureau took Duterte's statements seriously because of the potential threat to national security. The NBI director is the last prosecution witness on Duterte's alleged threats. LASCAÑAS AFFIDAVIT The prosecution also showed a 2011 video of Vice President Duterte punching a court sheriff when she was still Davao City mayor and featured an excerpt of alleged Davao Death Squad hitman Arturo Lascañas' affidavit on drug-related killings to repeated objections from defense counsel Mark Vinluan. Vinluan stressed the defense's objection to the Lascañas affidavit, which was submitted to the International Criminal Court but that Matibag had no personal knowledge on. "We cannot allow this witness to build his testimony based on this document," Vinluan also said, pointing out the affidavit is unsigned and was not notarized. Luistro said the video and the affidavit were material since the NBI considered these in its investigation. Matibag also referred to the affidavit as "open source intelligence" that the NBI used for leads. Escudero allowed the presentation of the affidavit but reminded senators that its contents were not necessarily true and that the impeachment court was not saying that they were. At a press briefing after the hearing, defense spokesperson Michael Poa declined to speculate on why prosecutors included the Lascañas statement but stressed its contents cannot be taken at face value. “Si Mr. Lascañas lang po ang puwedeng mag-identify ng sarili niyang affidavit and no one else,” he also said of the document, which was not notarized. Matibag later told the impeachment court that the NBI already has persons of interest — people who may be involved in an investigation but who are not suspects — but said he could not disclose who they are . "[U]nang-una pong mangyayari rito ay makokompromiso po ang ating imbestigasyon at mailalagay po sa alanganin yun pong ating mga tinatawag na informants o assets na nasa ground na nagbibigay sa atin ng human intel na tinatawag," he said. (First of all, it would compromsie the investigation and put our informants or assets on the ground giving us human [intelligence] at risk.) DEFENSE BRINGS UP MATIBAG'S WIFE, OPINION COLUMNS During cross-examination, Vinluan raised that Matibag is married to Laguna 1st District Rep. Ann Matibag, one of the House members who supported Duterte's impeachment. The NBI director said his wife's job "is totally detached" from his official duties. When confronted with opinion pieces critical of Duterte that he had written for The Daily Tribune as well as an art card showing the vice president has retained a high trust rating, Matibag said the NBI "cannot be swayed by public opinion [or our] personal opinion." He also told Vinluan that trust ratings in surveys are different from the public trust that the Articles of Impeachment allege Duterte broke. Matibag acknowledged that the Department of Justice, where the NBI filed its Inciting to Sedition and Grave Threats complaints against Duterte in February 2025, has yet to find basis for the allegation that the vice president actually contracted a killer. He said, though, that it is an open and continuing investigation. PIA CAYETANO SCOLDS PROSECUTION The defense asked to be allowed to continue cross-examination on Wednesday, giving senator-judges time to ask their own questions and to otherwise have the floor. Sen. Pia Cayetano, one of the few senators who are also lawyers, took Luistro to task for including the Lascañas affidavit that the defense had repeatedly objected to. She said the prosecution was "trying to prove something" by presenting the document and quoting from it even if Matibag had no personal knowledge on its contents and on how it was executed. She added that the quoted portion "cannot be unheard" even if Escudero had stressed that the affidavit's contents are hearsay. Cayetanos take impeachment issues to Facebook Live "Do your job and present the proper witness and the proper documentation to [prove your case]," she said in a rare raised voice in the trial day. — Jonathan de Santos, ABS-CBN News Trial resumes at 2 p.m. on Wednesday, July 22 MANILA — House prosecution legal spokesperson Atty. Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said on Tuesday that it is “normal” to interview witnesses before an impeachment trial. This was in response to the line of questioning by defense lawyer Attorney Mark Vinluan during the trial against Vice President Sara Duterte, which involved National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag. Vinluan asked Matibag, a witness, if he was briefed by Rep. Gerville Luistro when they met up before the trial. “And you are confirming in open court that you discussed or you were briefed in that meeting based on your testimony,” Vinluan said. This was met with a resounding expression of the word “Misleading!” from multiple individuals, seeming to come from the side where the prosecution sat. “Well, I'm a lawyer, and I know where you're going. There was no discussion or coaching,” Matibag replied. Tolosa stressed it is not irregular for a prosecutor to meet with a witness before they testify. “What he said is he had an opportunity to meet with the public prosecutor. But there is nothing unusual or irregular about that. Napakanormal ho ’yan sa lahat ng paglilitis – kahit sa normal na mga kaso. Normal ho ’yan. Bago ka mag-upo ng testigo, normal na kausapin mo, interview-hin mo ’yung witness para malaman mo ano bang masasabi niya dito sa paglilitis na ito,” Tolosa said. Observers from inside the session hall also caught wind of other events or reactions that may not have been seen on the livestream. Senate impeachment court presiding officer Senator Francis Escudero, Duterte’s lead counsel Atty. Sheila Sison, and House lead prosecutor and Batangas 2nd District Representative Gerville Luistro were spotted talking while the impeachment trial against Duterte was on recess. While the specific topic of discussion could not be heard from where observers stayed at the session hall, Escudero made reference to a discussion with counsel for the parties before the trial adjourned. Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri asked why the subpoenas for the appearance of former Land Bank branch managers Violeta Constantino and Nenita Camposano were to be withdrawn. “You are withdrawing the subpoena because you feel that we might not take them up tomorrow? [...] You mean, we cannot take it up tomorrow?” Zubiri asked. Escudero answered, “I would think so. That was pursuant to a discussion with both counsel for the parties earlier.” Only snippets of the conversation among Escudero, Sison, and Luistro could be heard, with the senator saying phrases such as, “I’m going to give you time to decide.” After adjournment, Tolosa, House prosecutor and Bicol Saro Representative Terry Ridon, and House prosecution panel spokesperson and Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Alonto Adiong held a press conference. However, they said they did not hear the conversation among the three. At many points throughout the trial, senator-judges temporarily exited the session hall. There were times when as few as 12 senators remained in their seats. At around 3:17 p.m., only Senators Escudero, Zubiri, Sherwin Gatchalian, Erwin Tulfo, Francis Pangilinan, Lito Lapid, Panfilo Lacson, JV Ejercito, Risa Hontiveros, Vicente Sotto III, Bam Aquino, and Pia Cayetano were still in the session hall. The number of senator-judges soon increased, but continued to fluctuate throughout the day. MANILA — National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag declined to identify the alleged "contracted assassin" and other persons of interest (POIs) linked to Vice President Sara Duterte during Tuesday's impeachment trial. Matibag was asked by the prosecution to identify the POIs but refused, citing the ongoing investigation. During a press conference after the hearing, Impeachment Court spokesperson Atty. Reginald Tongol was asked whether Matibag could disclose the identities of the POIs in an executive session. Tongol said such a scenario is possible, explaining that an executive session forms part of the Senate's legislative process and may be suppletorily applied under the Senate Impeachment Rules. “Base on my analysis of the rules po, under rule 6 of the senate impeachment rules, mababasa po ninyo doon na, suppletory applicable yung senate rules, pati po ng rules of court.” “Pag sinabi po nating suppletory applicable, pag hindi po sinasabi sa senate impeachment rules, yung mga ganung mga processo, pwede pang i-apply yung senate rules on the legislative process. Doon po may makikitang executive session at kung yun po yung balak gawin ng isang senator judge mag move po siya, then baka po viable possibility po yun na pwedeng mangyari.” Tongol noted, however, that none of the senator-judges has so far moved to hold an executive session for the possible disclosure of the identities of the persons of interest. He also reiterated that under Memorandum Circular No. 15, issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Matibag is bound by confidentiality rules and is prohibited from disclosing the identities of the persons of interest because they are part of an ongoing investigation. Footage of a 2011 incident in which Vice President Sara Duterte, then mayor of Davao City, punched a sheriff during a demolition of shanties in the city. Screenshot from ABS-CBN News Channel on YouTube/File MANILA — A 2011 incident in which Vice President Sara Duterte, then mayor of Davao City, punched a sheriff was raised Tuesday during the Senate impeachment trial of the country's second-highest official. Footage of a television news report on the incident was played during the proceedings as National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag took the witness stand. Matibag cited the incident as one of the cases the NBI considered in establishing what it described as a "pattern of violence" while investigating allegations of grave threats made by Duterte against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The confrontation, captured on video, occurred during a demolition operation in Davao City in 2011. The sheriff involved, Abe Andres, is also listed among the prosecution's witnesses in the impeachment trial. Aside from the video, the NBI also obtained an affidavit from Arturo Lascañas, a former police officer and self-confessed member of the vigilante group Davao Death Squad. In the affidavit, Lascañas described Duterte as among the architects of Oplan Tokhang, the controversial anti-illegal drug campaign carried out during the administration of former President Rodrigo Duterte, the Vice President's father, Matibag narrated during his testimony. Matibag is serving as the prosecution's final witness on allegations of grave threats and inciting to sedition, which form part of the Articles of Impeachment against Duterte. The article of impeachment is mainly anchored on statements made by Duterte in which she claimed to have instructed someone to kill Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and Speaker Martin Romualdez should she be killed first. It also cites remarks in which Duterte said she imagined beheading the President. LIVE UPDATES: Vice President Sara Duterte's Impeachment Trial (Day 8) RELATED VIDEOS The defense and House prosecution panels cross-examine NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag as he takes the witness stand during the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Matibag was asked about the agency’s ongoing investigation related to the fourth article of impeachment, focusing on the grave threats uttered by Duterte against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag on Tuesday said his job as bureau head, particularly in the probe into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., is “detached” from his wife being a House member. Matibag testified in Duterte’s impeachment trial in relation to the NBI’s investigation of her alleged “threats” against Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. During cross-examination, defense counsel Mark Vinluan raised that Matibag’s wife, Laguna Rep. Ma. Rene Ann Lourdes "Ann" Matibag, endorsed House Resolution No. 989 that set forth the Articles of Impeachment against the vice president. He said that he was testifying at the impeachment court because he had been summoned and by the invitation of the House impeachment panel. “However, the job of my wife as a legislator is totally detached from me being the director of the National Bureau of Investigation,” he said. The court did not issue a subpoena for Matibag, who later clarified that he is appearing “as a witness as called upon by this honorable court.” ‘PREMATURE, TRIAL BY PUBLICITY’ Vinluan asked whether Matibag’s testimony that the NBI has identified “persons of interest” in its probe is “premature,” after confirming that it is part of the standard operating procedure (SOP) to give Duterte a chance to be confronted with the findings. “Considering that you’re still pursuing those leads, don’t you think that your testimony today is premature?” Vinluan said. Matibag responded: “Hindi po. Sapagkat malinaw naman po sa statement ng ating bise presidente na meron siyang kinausap para patayin si Bongbong Marcos, si Liza Marcos Araneta, si Martin Romualdez." (No, because the vice president's statement that she had talked to someone to kill Bongbong Marcos, Liza Marcos Araneta and Martin Romualdez was clear.) He said Duterte's statement, made in a streamed online conference, was a "clear confession" by someone who had plans to have people killed.. Matibag: Sara Duterte remarks vs Marcos a threat to national security Vinluan also asked whether the agency is attempting trial by publicity. Matibag rejected this, citing NBI’s refusal to publicize the details of its investigation. Asked whether his testimony that the NBI has leads would prejudice the ongoing investigation, Matibag said he did not name the persons of interest precisely to avoid compromising an ongoing probe. LEAKED VIDEO Vinluan also raised a leaked video of an argument between Matibag and his friend, Mel Sabio, asking whether it demonstrated "an emotional outburst" on Matibag's part. In response, Matibag acknowledged that his statements in the video were made out of "galit at (anger and) disappointment," but said he has since regretted his remarks. Although the specific statements were not discussed during the hearing, reports said the recording captured Matibag threatening to kill Sabio. Vinluan also presented a Daily Tribune graphic showing the results of a recent Social Weather Stations survey , in which Duterte received a 57-percent public trust rating. Citing opinion pieces Matibag wrote for the same publication, including one in which he said public trust in the Vice President was crumbling, Vinluan asked whether he believed Duterte had betrayed public trust despite her high survey ratings. Matibag said surveys are merely "snapshots", saying also that the NBI "cannot be swayed by public opinion [or our] personal opinion." Matibag said public trust ratings in surveys are different from betrayal of public trust — an allegation in the Articles of Impeachment. "Kapag ating pinagbasehan ang popularidad, ibig sabihin ba nito, ang isang pinakakilala at popular na tao ay puwede nang gumawa ng krimen at hindi natin papapanagutin?" he said. (If our basis is popularity, does it mean that a well-known and popular person can commit a crime and not be held accountable?) 'Pattern of violence'? Duterte's sheriff-punching incident raised in impeachment trial ‘HEARSAY’ The defense also dismissed Matibag’s knowledge of the agency’s investigation into Duterte’s “grave threats” before his appointment as director February this year as “hearsay.” Matibag said he learned about the proceedings and findings through investigation reports and “upon the discussion of the investigating officers.” The counsel then cited the rules on evidence stating that “a witness can testify only to those facts which he or she knows of his or her personal knowledge that is, which are derived from his or her own perception.” Vinluan then said that a testimony, “if not based on personal knowledge, then that is hearsay.” WATCH

articles.title: NBI probes Taguig flood projects; DOJ says no order issued
articles.text:
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Monday said it started its investigation into flood control projects in Taguig City, even as the Department of Justice (DOJ) clarified Monday that it did not order the probe.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the bureau was already looking into 11 flood control projects implemented in 2022 that were allegedly linked to some of the country's top 15 contractors.

“In fact, we are already investigating, kasi nung 2022 merong 11 proyekto diyan na somehow related doon sa mga pinangalanan na Top 15 contractors,” Matibag told reporters.

(In fact, we are already investigating because, in 2022, there were 11 projects there that were somehow linked to those named among the top 15 contractors.)

“Baka sabihin ninyo timing na naman. Anyway, public na naman ‘yan dahil sinasabi ni Senator Lacson, so I think we should mention it,” he added.

(You might say this is about timing again. Anyway, this is already public knowledge because Senator Lacson mentioned it, so I think we should mention it.)

Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, however, stressed that the DOJ did not direct the NBI to conduct the investigation, saying the bureau was acting under its own mandate.

“We will respect the independence of the NBI relative to their mandate to pursue investigations. First thing, hindi ito pinag-utos ng DOJ. This is pursuant to the mandate of the NBI to pursue all this,” Vida said.

(We will respect the independence of the NBI in carrying out its mandate to pursue investigations. First, the DOJ did not order this. This is pursuant to the NBI's mandate to pursue these matters.)

Vida said that should the case reach the DOJ, the department would act based on the evidence presented.

“Kung sakaling makarating sa DOJ ‘yan, it will be based on what are the pieces of evidence presented. Rule of law pa rin tayo,” he said.

(If that reaches the DOJ, our action will be based on the evidence presented. We still abide by the rule of law.)

On Sunday, Senate Blue Ribbon Committee chairperson Senator Erwin Tulfo told fellow Senator Alan Peter Cayetano to be ready for an investigation into Taguig's flood control projects.

Cayetano's brother, former Taguig Mayor and current PTV general manager Lino Cayetano, who served as city mayor from 2019 to 2022, had sought an investigation into P6 billion worth of flood control projects implemented in Taguig from 2022 to 2025.

Vida also said ongoing investigations by other agencies should not be viewed as a distraction for senator-judges.

“Hindi dapat dahil ‘yung paghahabol natin ng accountability, hindi naman tumitigil ‘yun. Pare-parehong may ginagampanan, at ginagalang natin ang mga Senator-Judges,” Vida said.

(It should not be, because our pursuit of accountability does not stop. We all have our respective roles to play, and we respect the senator-judges.)

“And sa akin, kung wala namang dapat ipangamba about sa rule of law, wala dapat ipangamba ang mga senator-judges,” he added.

(And for me, if there is nothing to fear from the rule of law, then the senator-judges have nothing to fear.)

According to Vida, the NBI investigation is not yet barred by prescription, meaning authorities may still legally investigate and prosecute any alleged offenses arising from the projects. — MCG GMA News

articles.title: Matibag to shed light on probe into VP Sara Duterte's 'kill' threat — spox
articles.text:
National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is expected to shed light on the agency’s probe into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged death threat against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., when he testifies before the impeachment court on Tuesday, the prosecution panel said Sunday.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday, Atty. Benjamin Tolosa said Matibag is expected to provide key details that the first two witnesses could not cover due to the limited scope of their work.

“Lagi niya hong sinasabi [na] ang makakasagot diyan ay ‘yung intelligence service na, so diyan ho papasok si NBI Director Melvin Matibag,” Tolosa said, referring to the testimony of NBI Cybercrime Division chief Jeremy Lotoc.

(He kept saying that the intelligence service would be able to answer that, so that is where NBI Director Melvin Matibag comes in.)

“Siya ho ang makakapagbigay-linaw tungkol sa kung ano ang masusing imbestigasyon na ginawa ng NBI patungkol dito sa mamamatay-tao na kinausap ng bise presidente,” he added.

(He can shed light on the NBI’s thorough investigation into the alleged assassin whom the Vice President said she had spoken to.)

Tolosa also argued that the article of impeachment accusing Duterte of making grave threats against the President, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez could be supported by her own statements and her refusal to retract the alleged threat.

“Meron ba talagang kinausap na mamamatay-tao?... Napakaliwanag na po ng sagot diyan, meron. Ano ho ang pruweba natin? ‘Yung tinatawag na admission against interest ng bise presidente, sa kanya na po nanggaling 'yan,” Tolosa said.

(Did she really talk to an assassin? The answer to that is already very clear: yes. What is our proof? What we call the Vice President’s admission against interest—it came from her herself.)

Tolosa said an admission against interest is among the strongest forms of evidence under the Rules of Court because it comes directly from the person against whom it is being used.

“Lalo na dito, binigyan siya ng pagkakataon, three days after, para bawiin ito… pero hindi ho niya binawi yon. In fact, lalo pa niya hong diniin na talagang meron pero tinry ho lang niyang i-justify ‘yan by saying wala namang criminal act na revenge from the grave,” he said.

(Especially in this case, she was given an opportunity three days later to retract it, but she did not. In fact, she doubled down on it and merely tried to justify it by saying that there is no criminal act in seeking revenge from beyond the grave.)

Asked about the possibility that some senator-judges could question Matibag over the NBI’s separate investigation into alleged anomalies surrounding the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, Tolosa expressed confidence that the presiding officer would ensure that the proceedings remain focused on the impeachment case.

“At the end of the day, umaasa pa rin kami na tatalima pa rin ang mga senator-judges doon ho sa requirements under their own rules, not to unduly discriminate against anyone,” Tolosa said.

(At the end of the day, we still hope that the senator-judges will adhere to the requirements under their own rules and not unduly discriminate against anyone.)

On July 15, the NBI announced plans to create a task force to investigate alleged anomalies in the bidding and funding of projects related to the Philippines’ hosting of the 2019 SEA Games.

Senator Alan Peter Cayetano served as chairperson of the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), which organized the country’s hosting of the regional sporting event.

The NBI investigation has drawn scrutiny from Cayetano and Senators Pia Cayetano and Robin Padilla, who questioned its timing amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Duterte.— MCG GMA News

articles.title: NBI to file raps over P55 million SEAG cauldron
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said. Speaking at a forum in Quezon City over the weekend, Matibag said the investigation had yielded documents and testimonies that could support criminal charges. “Within the next few days, perhaps within a week, we will be filing cases,” Matibag said. The investigation is part of the NBI’s broader probe into the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), which Matibag said involves multiple cases and a large volume of documents and testimonies. “We divided this into pieces so we can file cases. There will be different cases coming out. The cauldron is another case. That might be the first one,” he said. Matibag said the NBI had obtained documents concerning the cauldron, which reportedly cost P55 million, although the actual cost was allegedly only about P5 million. He said several leaders of sports associations were also being investigated, with some already appearing before the NBI after receiving subpoenas. Matibag said the NBI was also examining the activities of people associated with Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano, who was the head of PHISGOC in 2019. He identified sports executive Ramon Suzara as among those being looked into, noting that some PHISGOC members had been Cayetano’s colleagues, staff members or associates. “We are still developing and checking what ventures they are involved in,” Matibag said. The NBI is also looking into why PHISGOC continued to sponsor international events despite being created specifically to organize the 2019 SEA Games. “It was supposed to end its existence after the SEA Games. But we found out that until now, they are still sponsoring international events. We are looking into that,” Matibag said. Matibag stressed that the PHISGOC investigation remains ongoing and that the NBI is pursuing separate cases based on the evidence it has gathered. articles.title: NBI chief Matibag did NOT step down
articles.text: Melvin Matibag stepped down from his post as director of the National Bureau of Investigation. As of May 21, Melvin Matibag continues to serve as NBI director. Reports that NBI agents who attempted to serve an ICC arrest warrant for Sen. Bato Dela Rosa “betrayed” him are false. A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post following the May 11 mayhem at the Senate involving an attempt to arrest Sen. Bato Dela Rosa. Not true. The NBI chief did not step down. The false claim originated from a YouTube channel that published a video on May 12 with a thumbnail that bore the text: “ MATIBAG BUMITAW NA. SENADO TINAPOS SI MATIBAG SA NBI? 9-NBI AGENT NILAGLAG SI MATIBAG (MATIBAG HAD STEPPED DOWN. SENATE ENDED MATIBAG AT NBI? 9 NBI AGENTS BETRAYED MATIBAG)” It surfaced the day after Dela Rosa appeared at the Senate for the first time since November 2025, when news came out that the International Criminal Court had issued a warrant for his arrest in connection with the crimes against humanity case in which the senator is named as a co-conspirator. NBI agents attempted to serve the arrest warrant, which prompted Dela Rosa to run, leading to a chase on a staircase from the parking area to the session hall, where the senator eventually obtained protective custody from Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano. Matibag continues to hold his position at the NBI. On May 21, he went to Legazpi City to lead the inauguration of the NBI Academy in the Bicol Region. The nine NBI personnel involved in chasing Dela Rosa were cited in contempt at the Senate and have since been turned over to the NBI as the bureau conducts its own investigation into the matter. There have been no reports from authorities or from the media that they “betrayed” Matibag in any way. The false claim gained attention anew after three other YouTube channels published their versions of the graphic from May 15 to 16 with some visual enhancements, such as adjusting saturation levels, blurring/unblurring some faces, and switching the placement of the text and pictures. Several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts then pushed out these graphics in the same time period, a few days after gunshots rang out within the Senate premises on the evening of May 13. Dela Rosa was then still under protective custody of the Senate. The publishers on FB notably used hashtags like #ddssolidsupporters #protectvpsarah (sic) and #pilipinasduterteparin. Four separate YouTube channels have used the false thumbnail for their videos, namely PINAS NEWS INSIDER (the original publisher), PINAS NEWS INSIGHT , KOMENTARYO PH, and KAPANIG NG MASA . Their clips have collectively gotten over 300,000 views, 16,000 likes, and 2,100 comments. VERA Files Fact Check has also flagged nine posts on FB that reposted the graphic. articles.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said. The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa. Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war. Dela Rosa left the Senate with Sen. Robinhood Padilla early on May 14. A DOJ special prosecutor panel later concluded that the Senate had not been under attack and that the actions of then-acting Senate sergeant-at-arms Mao Aplasca were not justified. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla dismissed Aplasca on June 25 for grave misconduct and gross neglect of duty over the shooting incident.? The ombudsman is expected to determine whether sufficient evidence exists to bring charges before the courts. articles.title: FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa did NOT surrender to NBI
articles.text: Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. No verified reports support claims that Dela Rosa surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said the lawmaker has yet to be apprehended, noting that a manhunt to locate dela Rosa is ongoing. Amid rumors of a supposed arrest, several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are capitalizing on posts claiming that Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The posts are untrue and designed to attract clicks for monetization. VERA Files traced the earliest copy of the claim to an Aug. 3 post by an FB page advocating for the 2028 presidential bid of Vice President Sara Duterte. It carried a photo set of the fugitive lawmaker interacting with men in uniform. The post also bore the caption, “Senator bato delarosà sumukó na [shocked emoji] Sa mga NBÎ at nag salita at humingi… (Senator Bato dela Rosa has surrendered to the NBI, spoke out, and pleaded…),” but ended with the phrase “see more,” creating the impression that additional details would follow. A tactic employed by some disinformation peddlers previously flagged by VERA Files, the teaser seemed intended to entice users to click the photo set, which contained an embedded link that redirects them to a product page on a popular e-commerce platform. No verified reports substantiate online claims that dela Rosa surrendered to the NBI. In fact, the agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said that the senator wanted by the ICC has yet to be apprehended, adding that their manhunt operation to locate dela Rosa is still ongoing. The photos used in the spurious posts appeared to be screenshots from a video originally posted by a certain Alvin Go on May 13, after the shooting incident in the Senate. In the clip , dela Rosa was seen shaking hands with a police officer, not an NBI agent or official. Notably, the fraudulent posts began circulating a day before the FB post of Jimmy Bondoc, one of dela Rosa’s counsels, saying: “Bad news is coming. Pray hard that it is not true, for the good of the nation.” The cryptic message, which can no longer be found on Bondoc’s official page, supposedly fueled speculations of dela Rosa’s arrest, according to some news reports . Dela Rosa has remained at large since May 14 following a gun-firing incident in the Senate as authorities earlier attempted to serve him the ICC warrant. The former police chief and enforcer of ex-president Rodrigo Duterte’s brutal anti-drug campaign is wanted by the international tribunal for the crime against humanity of murder in relation to the killing of at least 32 people between July 2016 and April 2018. From Aug. 3 to 5, VERA Files identified at least 34 FB posts spreading the untrue claim. Their closely spaced publication times—from as little as a minute to several hours apart—raise the possibility of coordinated activity. All posts used the photo set as a thumbnail to disguise affiliate links to several products on Lazada and Shopee, including food, cosmetics, phone cases, portable fans, and water tumblers. The links earn commissions for the accounts whenever netizens click and make purchases. As of writing, the clickbait posts by Inday sa 2028 (created on Oct. 23, 2022 as Ver0níca Kittty D. ), Kitty Duterte fanpage (July 11, 2023) and DU30 KITTY VEE (created on May 27, 2020 as Ｎａｔｈａｎ 願今。 ), among others, collectively garnered over 1,000 reactions. Another notable observation is a mismatch between the little to no interactions on posts from some of the documented FB pages and their thousands of followers. articles.title: Palace: Marcos Jr. won’t interfere with impeachment conviction threshold issue | ABS-CBN News
articles.text: Senator-judges listen to Attorney Karen Batu, Officer-in-Charge of the Records Division of the Office of the Ombudsman, as she takes the witness stand on the 25th day of the impeachment trial against Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on September 15, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA – Malacanang is taking a hands-off stance on the conviction threshold issue being tackled by the Senate impeachment court. Several legal luminaries or amici curiae (friends of the court) offered legal opinions on Wednesday to help the Senate impeachment court settle the least number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte. Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said she only heard of Retired Supreme Court Chief Justice Hilario Davide Jr.’s opinion that senators facing plunder charges or whose whereabouts are unknown should not be counted in determining the votes needed to convict an impeached official. Sara Duterte trial: What retired justices said on conviction threshold However, she maintained that the Palace would leave the issue up to the upper chamber. “Sa parte po ng administrasyon, sa parte po ng Pangulo, hindi po kami magbibigay ng anumang opinyon, ng anumang judgement patungkol po diyan. Hahayaan po natin ang Senado na siyang mag-determine kung ano sa palagay nila ang nararapat,” Castro said in a press briefing Wednesday, September 16. “Ang kailangan lamang po dito ay manaig ang hustisya at ang lahat ng serbisyong ginagawa naman natin ay para sa taumbayan, so doon lang po but kung ano po ang magiging threshold hindi po makikialam ang Pangulo patungkol diyan,” she added.
